dedupe_keys.name: usgs routine us mining seismicity catalogues mine explosions and roof collapses

description: This USGS resource covers seismic events caused by mining in the United States, mainly large routine explosions at surface mines and quarries and roof collapses induced by longwall coal mining. From May 1997 to July 2013 the National Earthquake Information Center produced separate monthly catalogues of these events, with phase arrival times in MCHEDR format from 1997 and ISF format from October 1999; since August 2013 mining events have been listed in the main online earthquake catalogue, found by selecting non-earthquake event types. Analysts identify events from their locations in mining districts, their time of day, since blasts are set off in daytime, and their seismic waveforms. It is produced by the U.S. Geological Survey. Coverage is national. The files and catalogue queries are free to download; no licence is stated, as usual for US Government works. Caveats: identification is provisional and based on indirect evidence, and only collapses large enough to be located appear. For simulation it separates mining events from natural earthquakes in hazard catalogues and documents ground shaking and collapses around mines, useful for hazard exposure studies of mines and nearby infrastructure. It is related to the St. Gallen geothermal induced seismicity case study record in this catalogue, another source on seismicity caused by industry.
